description: Repair guide content for offline use. Each guide has one optional illustration reference; steps contain text only. UI layout, navigation, and buttons are implemented separately in SwiftUI. The imageName values are asset-name placeholders and do not include actual image files.

problem.name: Bleach Marks
problem.description: Color loss or small bleached areas.

repair.title: REWORK THE MARK.
repair.summary: Bleach removes color. A decorative patch can hide a stable mark without applying more chemicals.
repair.bestFor: Clean, sturdy fabric with no thinning or holes.
repair.beforeYouBegin: Never apply more bleach. Do not patch fragile or chemically contaminated fabric.

steps.instruction: Check the care label. Make sure the marked fabric is still strong and dry.
Choose a washable patch that covers the discolored area with a margin.
Keep fabric layers separate; pin the patch flat and stitch around its edges.
Secure thread ends and check comfort before washing as the label allows.

problem.name: Stubborn Stains
problem.description: Marks that cannot be washed away.

repair.title: RECLAIM THE STAIN.
repair.summary: When a washable garment has a permanent cosmetic stain, disguise it using a decorative patch.
repair.bestFor: Clean, safe garment: stain is cosmetic, not a hazardous residue.
repair.beforeYouBegin: Do not conceal chemical contamination. Delicate fabrics may need professional care.

steps.instruction: Follow the care label first. Do not work on contaminated or unwashed items.
Choose a suitable patch larger than the visible stain.
Protect the second fabric layer and sew the patch around all sides.
Check that the patch is secure and the garment remains comfortable.

problem.name: Small Tears & Holes
problem.description: Minor tears, punctures or tiny holes.

repair.title: MEND IN PLAIN SIGHT.
repair.summary: Give a small tear a new personality with a visible, reinforced hand-sewn patch.
repair.bestFor: Small opening with sturdy surrounding fabric; not on safety-critical seams.
repair.beforeYouBegin: Handle needles carefully. Large, stretched or load-bearing tears need expert repair.

steps.instruction: Lay the garment flat and inspect the tear and surrounding fabric.
Cut a similar-weight backing patch slightly larger than the opening.
Keep layers separate and secure the patch with small, even stitches.
Fasten thread ends and gently check the repair for loose edges.

repair.title: BUTTONS & SEAMS.
repair.summary: Reattach a button or secure a loose seam with simple hand stitches.
repair.bestFor: Garments with sturdy fabric around the button or seam.
repair.beforeYouBegin: Handle needles carefully and make sure the fabric around the repair is strong.

steps.instruction: For a loose seam, turn the garment inside out and align the edges.
For a button, place the replacement where the original sat.
Stitch through the holes several times and knot the thread securely.
For a seam, use small backstitches and secure both ends.
